youtube.description: In this episode you will explain what with really does, write __enter__ and __exit__ and use contextlib.contextmanager, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Set up and tidy up · 1:06 Enter and exit · 1:47 Door in, door out · 2:22 Second program · 3:28 Recap · 4:02 Bug of the Day · 4:50 Challenge · 5:10 Next episode

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: You have used with for files. Today we learn what happens behind it, and build our own.

scenes.onScreen: "Set up and tidy up": three numbered lines (1. __enter__ runs when the with block starts; 2. __exit__ runs when the block ends, even on error; 3. @contextmanager makes one from a generator) and an analogy card: a hotel room: the key card opens the door on the way in, and the room is cleaned on the way out, whatever happened inside
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A with statement guarantees a cleanup. Behind it, Python calls two special methods. Dunder enter runs at the start, and its return value is tied to the name after as. Dunder exit runs at the end, even if an error happened inside. If exit returns True, the error is swallowed. If it returns False, the error continues. The contextlib module offers a shortcut, with a generator and one yield. Think of a hotel room. The key card opens the door on the way in, and the room is cleaned on the way out.

scenes.onScreen: A room with an entry door that rings a bell and an exit door that cleans the room, even when a red error arrow appears inside
scenes.animation: A room with two doors; a bell rings at the entry door, a cleaner at the exit door; a red lightning arrow inside still ends at the exit door
scenes.narration: Here is the picture. The with statement walks through the entry door, which calls enter. Your block runs inside the room. When the block ends, normal or with an error, Python always walks through the exit door, and calls exit. That is why with is trusted for files. Even if the code inside crashes, the file is closed on the way out.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One: with calls dunder enter at the start and dunder exit at the end. Two: dunder exit runs even when the block raises an error. Three: Returning True from dunder exit swallows the error. Four: at contextmanager builds one from a generator with one yield. Pause the video, and say these ideas out loud, once, slowly.

lines: With calls __enter__ at the start and __exit__ at the end.
__exit__ runs even when the block raises an error.
Returning True from __exit__ swallows the error.
@contextmanager builds one from a generator with one yield.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: __exit__ swallows the error
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. The block divides by zero. But our exit returns True. That tells Python, I handled it. The error vanishes, and the program prints finished. A real bug is now invisible. Return False, or nothing at all, and the error continues up to where you can catch it.

props.why: If exit returns True, Python treats the error as handled and hides it. Return False, or return nothing, so errors are never swallowed by accident.

scenes.onScreen: Why did the context manager never forget anything? It always cleaned up after itself.

shorts.title: What with does
shorts.script: The with statement guarantees a cleanup. Python calls dunder enter when the block starts. It calls dunder exit when the block ends, even if an error happened inside. That is why with is the safe way to open files. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: With always cleans up.

shorts.title: Write your own
shorts.hook: "To write your own context manager, make a class with two methods."
shorts.script: To write your own context manager, make a class with two methods. Enter does the setup. It returns the value that the name after as gets. Exit does the cleanup. Now with your class gives the same safety as with open. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Make your own.

shorts.title: The shortcut
shorts.script: The contextlib module has a shortcut. Write a generator with one yield, and add at contextmanager. Everything before the yield is the setup. Everything after it, in a finally block, is the cleanup. Short and tidy. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: A shortcut with yield.

shorts.title: Swallowed error
shorts.script: A dangerous bug. Dunder exit returns True. Python takes that to mean, I handled the error. Your divide by zero disappears, and the program says finished. Return False, or nothing, so errors are never swallowed by accident. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Never swallow errors.
